hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: Trump sends Witkoff and Kushner to Putin, then on to Kyiv
brief.h: The two envoys fly Friday, meet Putin in Moscow on Saturday and Zelensky in Kyiv on Sunday - their first visit to Ukraine of this term - carrying what Trump calls a proposal to end the war, with Moscow publicly cool on the Kyiv leg and people close to the Kremlin briefing that expectations are extremely low.
brief.t: Read the itinerary, not the announcement. Moscow first and Kyiv second is a sequencing choice that tells you where the terms are being written and who is being handed a text rather than drafting one, and Russia's reported lobbying to drop the Kyiv stop entirely says the Kremlin prefers a bilateral channel to a trilateral one. This is the same pair who have flown to Russia repeatedly - including a four-hour night session with Putin in January - and have never once landed in Ukraine, which is itself the map of the mediation. A trip is not a term sheet: the observable that would matter is whether anyone tables a ceasefire-in-place text with a line on it.
brief.context: The rail here is older than this weekend. Since the 2025 minerals framework, Washington's Ukraine file has been run out of an envoy channel staffed by dealmakers rather than the State Department's Europe bureau, and the currency on the table has consistently been reconstruction, resources and the roughly $300bn of frozen Russian sovereign assets held in Europe - money Brussels, not Washington, controls, which is why the Europeans keep discovering they are a party to a deal they are not in the room for. The deciding desk is the Kremlin's, because Russia is the side that can end this unilaterally and has not. Base rate: envoy shuttles that begin in the aggressor's capital with no published framework almost never produce a signed instrument on the first pass; they produce a readout. What would change the read is a dated, written ceasefire line that both delegations acknowledge in public.

angles.effect: Gains a visible peace process eight weeks before a midterm at the cost of two plane tickets, and can attribute failure to either capital.
Gains the thing he wants most from any process - direct great-power negotiation over Ukraine's head - and pays only in atmospherics while the strike tempo continues.
Pays first: he receives on Sunday a proposal drafted elsewhere and already shown in Moscow, and must reject it publicly or own it.
Pay in optionality - the frozen assets they hold are being spent rhetorically in a room they do not sit in.

dec.kill: A published ceasefire text with a demarcation line that both Moscow and Kyiv acknowledge - or conversely the Kyiv leg being cancelled at Russian request. Either settles whether this is mediation or a bilateral channel with a stopover.

consp.claim: That the peace mission is a business transaction wearing a diplomatic suit - the circulating version is that two real-estate men are flying to Moscow to negotiate access to roughly $300bn in frozen Russian assets and a multi-trillion-dollar reconstruction and minerals pot, and that ending the war is the by-product rather than the objective. It runs under the label peace for profit.
consp.spread: Loud and cross-spectrum: written up by the Daily Beast and IBTimes off a leaked plan, echoed in Kyiv Post's own editorial telling the envoys their visit is unwelcome unless they arrive with something, and repeated on /pol/'s /uhg/ and /chug/ Ukraine generals from opposite directions.
consp.read: This maps onto the oldest frame in the file - that mediation is cover for extraction - and unusually it has a checkable kernel rather than a vibe. A US-Ukraine reconstruction and investment fund with access to critical minerals genuinely exists and was signed in 2025, and the Dmitriev proposal to recycle frozen Russian central bank assets into joint US-Russian projects was actually reported. What the narrative adds, and cannot show, is causal direction: a profit motive being present is not the same as it being decisive, and the boring explanation - that this administration monetises everything it touches by habit - predicts exactly the same evidence.

brief.head: Norway seizes a Russian ship at Svalbard over Ukraine's $4.2bn award
brief.h: The Professor Molchanov, a 43-year-old Roshydromet research vessel that ferries staff and cargo to the Russian coal settlement of Barentsburg, was arrested there on 2 September on a Nord-Troms district court order of 31 August enforcing Naftogaz's $4.22bn Hague award for assets expropriated in Crimea; Putin, speaking in Vladivostok, called it state terror.
brief.t: The instrument is the story. Nobody is recovering $4.22bn from a four-decade-old Finnish-built survey ship - what was recovered is a precedent, in the one place on earth where a Russian state hull predictably sits inside a NATO member's jurisdiction. Call the mechanism ARBITRATION ENFORCEMENT: an award won at The Hague in 2023, confirmed enforceable by a Dutch court in late 2024, now converted into a physical arrest by a district judge in northern Norway. It is slower than a sanction and far harder to reverse, because it does not run through a foreign ministry that can be lobbied. Note Oslo's careful defence - that Norwegian officials merely executed a court order for a private claimant - which is legally accurate and politically useless in Moscow.
brief.context: Svalbard is governed by the 1920 treaty that grants Norway sovereignty while giving every signatory, Russia included, equal rights of access and commerce - which is exactly why Russia maintains a loss-making coal town at Barentsburg, and why every Norwegian administrative act there is read in Moscow as treaty erosion rather than housekeeping. The deciding desk was a court, not a cabinet, which is what makes it durable and what makes retaliation awkward: there is no minister to sanction. The Russian foreign ministry's chosen framing - that its citizens at Barentsburg are now effectively under blockade - is the tell for where pressure goes next, because resupply, not law, is Barentsburg's real vulnerability. Base rate: enforcement against sovereign assets captures symbols far more often than value, and is answered by counter-seizure rather than by payment. What would change the read is the confrontation moving from the courtroom to the sea lane.

angles.effect: Gain proof the award is live and executable, which raises the arrest risk on every Russian state hull entering a European port.
Pays the exposure - it now owns a standing confrontation on an archipelago it polices with a coast guard, adjacent to Russia's Kola bastion.
Gains a genuine treaty grievance and a sympathetic domestic story, and pays in access, since every future sailing to Svalbard now carries seizure risk.
Pay directly and have no seat: their resupply and rotation ran through the vessel now impounded at their own pier.

dec.kill: Russia answering through an appeal rather than through the Barents Sea. A counter-seizure of Norwegian assets, an interruption of Barentsburg resupply, or a Northern Fleet movement would mean the legal frame has been abandoned.

consp.claim: That the seizure is a manufactured pretext - the circulating reading is that a legal-looking arrest at Svalbard is the opening move in a Western plan to start boarding Russia's shadow-fleet tankers under colour of law, with a NATO-Russia incident in the Barents as the intended rather than accidental outcome.
consp.spread: Pro-Russia analysis Substacks that had already run the identical frame on Scandinavia's drone scare, amplified on X, and picked up on /pol/'s /chug/ general, which is treating the seizure as staged provocation.
consp.read: This is the pretext frame, the most reusable narrative in the Russia file, applied to every Arctic incident regardless of facts. The kernel is real and not itself a conspiracy: Europe has openly spent two years hunting for lawful ways to interdict the shadow fleet, and an arbitration warrant is a cleaner hook than a sanctions inspection. What the theory must assert without evidence is coordination - that a Naftogaz enforcement application filed through a Norwegian district court was timed by someone else for that purpose.

brief.head: US used Nvidia chips as leverage to close Armenia-Azerbaijan deal
brief.h: The Wall Street Journal reported Friday that the promise of American AI processors helped seal the Trump-brokered peace between Yerevan and Baku; on the public record, Firebird won a licence to export 6,144 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs to Armenia for a $500m facility, since announced as scaling toward $4bn and 50,000 GPUs.
brief.t: Name the mechanism and the whole thing becomes legible: THE COMPUTE PERMIT. An export licence costs Washington nothing appropriated, is revocable at will, and buys behaviour that used to require troops, treaties or aid money - so the export-control machinery built to deny chips to China is now being run in reverse, as a positive inducement. Armenia paid in alignment rather than cash: it signed the framework with Azerbaijan, accepted the TRIPP transit corridor across its own territory, and stepped visibly out of Moscow's security orbit. Pashinyan has said openly that he lobbied Trump personally to speed the licence through, which is the honest confirmation that the chips were a lever and not a reward.
brief.context: The rail predates the crisis, which is why a planned-design read survives here: the licensing regime, the Bureau of Industry and Security caseload and the diaspora-funded data-centre project all existed before the White House signing, and the peace text merely gave them something to be exchanged for. The deciding desk is BIS at Commerce, not State - which is also the vulnerability, because a licence granted by an agency can be pulled by the same agency once the corridor is built. The losers are unnamed in the announcement and obvious on a map: Russia loses the transit monopoly that made it indispensable to both capitals, and Iran loses a northern border it spent a decade keeping closed, and has already objected to the corridor. Base rate: technology-linked commitments are cheap to promise and slow to deliver, and phase one was only ever slated for the second quarter of 2026. Convert the slogan into units - 6,144 GPUs is a serious regional facility and a rounding error against a hyperscaler, so this buys Armenia relevance, not parity.

angles.effect: Gains a corridor across the South Caucasus and a client in Yerevan for the price of an export licence and roughly $200m of enterprise-fund seed money - the cheapest strategic entry on the board.
Gains compute, investment and a Western patron, and pays in dependency: the lever that opened the door can close it, and the corridor runs across its own territory.
Gains the connection to Nakhchivan it fought a war for, wrapped in an American brand rather than a Russian one.
Pay the whole bill with no seat: both lose a veto over movement across the Caucasus that neither has been without since the Soviet collapse.

dec.kill: The GPUs never physically landing and racking in Armenia, or the phase-two $4bn expansion never reaching a signed contract - either would mean the promise was the instrument and delivery was never the point.

brief.head: Blowout jobs report puts a September Fed hike back on the table
brief.h: Payrolls rose 162,000 in August against a consensus near 55,000, unemployment held at 4.1 per cent and June and July were revised up by a combined 55,000 - and within hours Trump was again demanding rate cuts.
brief.t: This is not really a labour-market story, it is a story about who owns the price of money. A committee that hikes eight weeks before a midterm, into a president publicly demanding the opposite, is the cleanest test of central-bank independence available in this cycle - and it now rests almost entirely on one number, because the employment side of the argument was settled this morning. Keep the disconfirming figure in view rather than the headline: average hourly earnings are up just 3.1 per cent year on year, and Jefferies' Thomas Simons reads the print as payback for three weak months rather than acceleration. A strong labour market with soft wages is not obviously an inflation emergency.
brief.context: The clock is the analysis: CPI lands on 11 September, the FOMC meets 15-16 September, the midterms are on 3 November. The rail underneath is that this administration has already politicised the series it is now citing - the BLS commissioner was fired in August 2025 over an accusation that the numbers were faked - which leaves the White House arguing that a strong print from an agency it purged proves the economy is booming, while simultaneously demanding emergency-style cuts. Those two claims do not sit together, and the distance between them is the analysis. The deciding desk is the FOMC, and the base rate is that a single payroll surprise almost never decides a meeting; the inflation print does. What would change the read is a hot CPI on 11 September, which converts a live possibility into a near-certainty.

angles.effect: Gains a boom narrative to campaign on and simultaneously loses its best argument for cuts - a strong economy is the worst possible case for emergency easing.
Gains cover to move on inflation and pays in political exposure, since any decision now will be read as partisan whichever way it goes.
Pay directly if the hike lands, and have no seat at either table.
Gain from a committee that is seen to decide on data - the independence premium is priced in the long end, not in the headline rate.

dec.kill: A soft 11 September CPI. If inflation improves, Governor Waller has already said he would lean to holding, and the hike case collapses regardless of the payroll number.

consp.claim: That the official numbers describe an economy nobody is actually living in - the circulating claim is that the print is produced for the campaign, with the boards posting personal counter-evidence instead: rent raised on the landlord's stated grounds of higher energy prices, and a heavily reposted thread arguing wage earners are about to snap because conditions are far grimmer than any release admits.
consp.spread: Several /pol/ threads running to three figures of replies, plus the /biz/ stock-market generals, where the Friday edition ran under the header bull market despite two massive wars.
consp.read: This is the lived-experience-versus-aggregate frame, the most durable narrative in economics because it is half true by construction: a national average genuinely cannot describe an individual budget, and energy-driven housing costs are real. The kernel is sharper than usual here - the BLS commissioner really was fired in 2025 over a faking accusation, and cumulative revisions since have taken roughly 79,000 jobs back out of the record - so the distrust has an evidentiary basis, even though today's print was revised up rather than down.

brief.head: Costa Rica's president opens the door to US military operations
brief.h: Laura Fernandez, in office since May, said American operations against transnational crime would obviously be very good for national security - while stressing that none are planned and that the Legislative Assembly would have to approve any of them.
brief.t: The significance is the identity of the speaker, not the strength of the statement. Costa Rica abolished its army in 1949 and has spent seventy-seven years making that the centre of its national brand, so a Costa Rican president discussing foreign forces on national territory at all is the signal; the caveats are the normal price of saying it out loud. Read it against the Caribbean campaign rather than as a domestic story - an air and maritime interdiction tempo around Venezuela is a logistics problem before it is a military one, and every willing government between Panama and Colombia shortens the chain. Constraint before character: Fernandez is not an ideological Atlanticist, she is a security-mandate president whose country's homicide rate doubled in a decade to 17.2 per 100,000, and who won an election fought on exactly that.
brief.context: The rail is constitutional. The 1949 charter abolished the standing army, and any foreign military presence requires legislative authorisation - which makes the Assembly, not the presidency, the deciding desk, and hands Washington a veto player it cannot lobby directly. That is the difference between this and the access arrangements the US already runs elsewhere in the isthmus. The wider machine is the one the region has watched all year: an interdiction campaign long on strikes and short on basing, where each new access agreement makes the next strike cheaper. Base rate: presidential openness expressed in an interview converts into an actual access agreement rarely and slowly - the observable is a bill, not a quote. What would change the read is a named facility or a tabled authorisation.

angles.effect: Gains the option value of a Central American access point at zero cost, since an expression of openness commits nobody and can be cited to third countries as momentum.
Gains a security-credibility signal with an electorate that elected her on crime, and pays if the Assembly refuses and she ends up weaker than before she spoke.
Pays first and quietly - the seventy-seven-year claim to be the country without an army now survives a public debate about hosting someone else's.
Pays the strategic cost: every additional willing government in the isthmus narrows the gap between an announced campaign and a sustainable one.

dec.kill: An authorisation actually tabled in the Legislative Assembly, or a named airfield or port. Absent either by year-end, this was an interview answer and not a policy.

watch: The Bab al-Mandab transit count, because it is now arguing against us. Lloyd's List Intelligence, publishing JMIC data, logged 202 traceable transits between 24 and 30 August against at least 302 the week before, a 273-a-week average from 27 July to 23 August, and 319 before the Saudi naval ban. Our standing read is a discriminating blockade aimed at Saudi-linked tonnage rather than a closed gate; a second consecutive week near 200 kills it, and a recovery above 273 restores it

Whether the envoy plane actually lands - Moscow on Saturday, Kyiv on Sunday. This is our own dated falsifier on GEO-005, running to 14 September. A trip is still not a term sheet, and the observable that matters more is whether anyone tables a ceasefire-in-place text with a demarcation line both delegations acknowledge in public

The CPI print on 11 September, then the 15-16 September FOMC. After 162,000 jobs against a consensus near 55,000, with unemployment steady at 4.1 per cent and 55,000 of upward revisions, the labour side of the argument is settled and the hike case rests entirely on inflation - Governor Waller has already said he would lean to holding if the number improves

Whether Russia answers Svalbard in court or in the Barents. Watch for a counter-seizure of Norwegian assets, an interruption of Barentsburg resupply now that Arktikugol's link vessel is impounded at its own pier, or Northern Fleet movement - and watch whether the NATO maritime patrol flights off the Kola bases, reported by Aftenposten from Flightradar24 data, become routine or stop

Whether the Armenian GPUs physically land and rack. The instrument was an export licence for 6,144 Nvidia Blackwell units, with a phase two announced at $4bn and 50,000 GPUs; a signed phase-two contract and installed hardware would mean the compute permit is a real currency, while a quiet lapse would mean the promise was always the whole product
lesson: Today's mechanism is eighty years old and it explains the diesel price better than any headline about tankers. In 1945 the economist Albert Hirschman published National Power and the Structure of Foreign Trade, and his argument was deceptively simple: the power one country holds over another is not measured by how much trade flows between them, but by how HARD it would be for the weaker side to replace it. Volume is not leverage. Substitutability is leverage. Apply that to oil and the whole story flips. Crude is highly substitutable - there are dozens of producers, and a barrel from Guyana burns much like a barrel from Basra - which is why the crude price is around $96 and calm-ish while the world's most important strait is contested. Refining capacity is NOT substitutable, because you cannot buy a distillation and hydrocracking unit off a shelf, and that is why the margin for turning crude into diesel just printed an all-time record of $108 a barrel while crude did not. Hirschman's prediction, restated for today, is that political power is quietly migrating to whoever controls the least substitutable step in the chain - which right now is not the oilfield but the refinery, and increasingly a refinery in India, the Gulf or China rather than in the West. It also predicts the behaviour we are watching: Russia banning diesel exports, Ukraine bombing refineries rather than wells, and Washington leaning on allies about a strait, are all the same move made from different seats - each side reaching for the bottleneck rather than the volume. Handle the theory honestly: Hirschman was writing about interwar German trade policy and his index has real limits, chiefly that it assumes states can perceive their own dependence, which they routinely cannot until the bill lands. But the test is scoreable and it is on our board as GEO-026 - if the diesel crack falls back under $45 before mid-December, the bottleneck was temporary and the leverage was borrowed; if it does not, the West has discovered a dependency it had not priced.

events.label: Strait of Hormuz
events.note: The chokepoint behind the diesel record: roughly 900,000 barrels a day of diesel and 350,000 of jet fuel normally leave the Gulf through here, and that flow has been disrupted since the war began on 28 February. No new confirmed hull strike reported today

events.label: Kharg Island
events.note: Still undamaged and still the subject of the 30 September falsifier clock. Handles about 90 per cent of Iranian crude exports; the March raid hit military sites here and deliberately spared the loading terminals

events.label: Ali al-Taher ridge, Lebanon
events.note: Katz says the capture of this high ground near Nabatieh completes the phase of securing control in the security zone, and that Israel will not withdraw until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout Lebanon - a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to meet

events.label: New York Harbor / Linden, NJ
events.note: The delivery point for the US diesel contract, and the tightest barrel in the world right now: East Coast distillate stocks at a record-low 19.3 million barrels in the week to 28 August, with the heating season still ahead

events.label: Ryazan refinery belt
events.note: Ukraine's drone campaign against Russian refining has been sustained enough that Moscow banned diesel exports through 30 September - one of the three simultaneous pulls on world distillate, and the one with a published expiry date

events.label: Moscow
events.note: Witkoff and Kushner are reported by TASS to arrive 5-6 September, the first dated meeting since February. Peskov declined to confirm; Moscow is reported to be resisting the onward leg to Kyiv, which is the informative detail

events.label: Kyiv

quiz.q: Crude is around $96 and off its highs, but the diesel refining margin just printed an all-time record of $108 a barrel. What does that combination actually tell you?
options: That there is less oil in the ground than the market believed
That the binding shortage is in refining capacity, not in crude - and refineries take years to build, so the constraint cannot be surged away
That speculators have cornered the diesel market
That OPEC has secretly cut production
quiz.why: A crack spread is the margin between a barrel of crude and the fuel refined out of it. When that margin sets records while the crude price does not, the scarce thing is the kit, not the geology - and that distinction is the whole story, because valves open in hours and refineries take years.

quiz.q: Katz said Israel will not leave southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout Lebanon. Why did the brief treat that sentence as the important one?
options: Because it is a threat to invade Beirut
Because it means Israel will withdraw within months
Because it violates the ceasefire text
Because it is a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to deliver, which turns a withdrawal into something that happens by decision rather than by completion
quiz.why: Watch the exit criterion, not the map. A condition no one can satisfy is not a milestone - it is an open-ended presence with a milestone's grammar, which is exactly how the 1985-2000 security zone worked.

quiz.q: The brief CUT the odds of an Israel-Hezbollah multi-week campaign on the day Israel declared a permanent security zone. What was the reasoning?
options: Because a held buffer historically produces chronic low-grade attrition instead of episodic campaigns - the 1985-2000 zone produced about two multi-week operations in fifteen years
Because Hezbollah has been destroyed
Because the ceasefire now has a third-party verifier
Because Israel's election makes any operation impossible
quiz.why: That base rate is roughly 13% a year for the escalation class, well below the 32% the book was carrying - and publishing a cut on an escalatory-sounding day is the test of whether a forecast follows evidence or mood.

quiz.q: Russia is reported to be trying to stop the US envoys continuing from Moscow to Kyiv. What does that behaviour most likely reveal?
options: That Russia is close to accepting a ceasefire
That Russia does not want to negotiate at all
That Moscow values exclusive access to the channel more than it values the meeting - a bargaining position rather than a peace position
That the envoys are working for Ukraine
quiz.why: Wanting the conversation to itself is a strong tell about intent. A party genuinely seeking convergence wants both sides in the room; a party seeking terms wants to speak to the guarantor alone.

quiz.q: CRITICAL THINKING. A widely shared claim says the diesel shortage is engineered - that US refineries were deliberately allowed to decay until scarcity was inevitable, and that America is exporting fuel out of a shortage. Which observable would most usefully test it?
options: Whether pundits on TV admit refining is a problem
Whether diesel prices go higher next month
Whether the government denies the claim
Whether the timeline of refinery closures predates the actors being blamed, and whether closure decisions track margins and complexity economics rather than any policy date
quiz.why: The checkable half of the claim is real - export flows and stretched maintenance intervals are documented. The engineered half needs a rail older than the crisis, and refinery closures driven by margin economics over four decades do not supply one. Testing a claim means finding the part that could fail, not the part that feels true.

plumbing.read: Today the physical leg and the monetary leg pointed the same way for the first time this week, and that is what makes it worth writing down. The physical print: US diesel at a record $5.820 a gallon, the crack at an all-time $108.02 intraday, East Coast distillate at a record-low 19.3 million barrels, August national stocks the thinnest since 1982. The monetary print: 162,000 August payrolls against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, into a Federal Reserve whose live debate is a rate RISE rather than a cut, and Waller leaning to hold only if inflation keeps improving. That combination is the manual's RESCUE WITHHELD class - a market certain the firemen are coming, in a shock the firemen cannot fix, because a policy rate does not build a hydrocracker. The long end has already priced it: ten-year 4.79%, thirty-year 5.27%, both above our published red lines, with the reverse-repo buffer at $0.70bn and effectively gone. What is STILL not printing is the milkshake tape - the broad dollar is 118.75 and soft on the month, so this remains a term-premium and supply-shock event rather than a dollar squeeze, and we say so rather than reaching for the more dramatic reading. Falsifier, dated: a diesel crack back under $45 before 15 December with the strait still contested marks this an outage, not a regime, and scores GEO-026 against us.
